classification.distribution: Cultivated in northwestern India and widely grown elsewhere

identification.description: Cylindrical yellowish-brown roots and stolons with longitudinal striations, fibrous fracture and intensely sweet taste.
identification.whole_plant: Perennial herb with erect branched stems.
identification.root: Yellowish-brown cylindrical roots and stolons; sweet taste and characteristic odour.
identification.leaf: Imparipinnate leaves with numerous oval leaflets and a terminal leaflet.
identification.flower: Small bluish to violet papilionaceous flowers in axillary spikes.
identification.bark: Thin root bark; pharmacognostic examination of the root/stolon is important.

therapeutics.precautions: Prolonged or high intake of glycyrrhizin-containing preparations may cause sodium retention, hypokalaemia and blood-pressure effects; use cautiously in susceptible individuals.
therapeutics.contraindications: Avoid unsupervised prolonged/high-dose use in hypertension, significant cardiovascular/renal disease or hypokalaemia.

nighantu_references: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Haritakyadi Varga; exact verse/edition requires verification
reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Glycyrrhizin content varies by root material and preparation; safety considerations are particularly relevant to concentrated extracts.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Licorice has been studied for demulcent, gastrointestinal and respiratory applications, but effects and safety depend on preparation, dose and duration.
modern_information.safety_notes: Glycyrrhizin-containing products can cause mineralocorticoid-like adverse effects with excessive or prolonged use.
